name: Superlove

_comment_shadow: No drop shadow on the type. The slab under it is opaque and the
glow under that is what lifts the whole thing off the photo, so a
shadow would only be a smudge inside an object that already has an
_comment_layout: The one channel that is NOT justified. Every other channel fits
each line to the full width at its own size, so the block comes out
with two straight edges; here the whole block is set at one size
and a short line is allowed to be short, centred over the lines
The slab is what makes the difference. Justified, it is a plain
rectangle and the type inside it has to be resized line by line to
keep it one; unjustified, the slab takes the shape of the words —
stepping in and out around a short line — and that silhouette is
the thing this channel is recognisable by. It also means the type
keeps one size, so nothing is enlarged for the sake of the edge.
_comment_outline: The keyline between the white letters and the slab. Thin on
purpose — it is there to stop the two reading as one another,
not to be seen as an outline.
_comment_sticker: The second, much wider outline, drawn under the letters and under
their keyline. At 25px it runs into itself between neighbouring
letters and between the lines, so the strokes stop being outlines
and become one solid block with the type cut into it.
The gradient is mapped across that whole block, corner to corner:
bottom-left to top-right, in three bands rather than one even
fade. Red is the block's own colour and holds flat across the
middle 30%; the corners take 35% each, one coming up out of the
pale pink and one dropping into the deep red. Keeping a flat band
in the middle at all is the point — a wash between the same three
colours over the whole run would leave no field of red anywhere,
only a different colour in every letter.
_comment_glow: Built the way the Karens halo is — the shape drawn again underneath
and blurred, stacked three times so the falloff stays soft while
the core gains body — but written out here rather than taken from
the `karen-glow` preset.
It started as that preset with overrides, and the overrides ate it:
different colour, different opacity, different radius, with only
the layer count left in common. A preset is for one design two
channels share, and this is no longer that design — sharing it
would only mean each channel's halo could be changed by an edit
aimed at the other one. Karens keeps the preset untouched.
The radius is 15 against Karens' 55, and the gap is not as wide as
it looks: this halo is thrown by the SLAB and not by the letters
(what the renderer does wherever a sticker exists, since the slab
is the shape on screen and so the shape the light comes off), so it
starts from a shape 25px larger in every direction. It is meant to
read as light coming off the block, not as weather around it — the
block already has an edge of its own, and all this has to do is put
it in front of the photo rather than printed on it.
The number that was actually chosen is the REACH: 19px of visible
light past the slab, which 15 happens to produce. Radius is not a
good handle on this halo, because `layers` stacks three passes at
full opacity and each one re-darkens the faint outer edge of the
one below into visibility — so the light carries about a quarter
further than the radius alone suggests, and halving the radius does
not halve what anyone sees. Anything that changes `layers` or
`opacity` changes the reach too, and the reach is the thing this
channel was tuned by.
_comment_highlight: This channel has no highlight feature. Every line gets the same
treatment — white on the one slab — and there is nothing a
highlighted line could be that would not just look like a mistake
in the block. `null` says so outright, and the Highlight Line
buttons go dead for it rather than doing nothing visible.

_comment_branding: Title left, subject right — what the automatic framing already
produces, so neither flip is needed.
No dark gradient behind the title, which is the one place this channel
departs from the default. The gradient exists to hold white type off a
bright photo; here the type is on an opaque slab that does that job
completely, so all a gradient would add is a dark smear across the
photo beside it. Per frame it is still a button away.
